# SetLayout

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Output` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public static class SetLayout
```

The parts a cooked Set is made of, named once.

## Remarks

**This exists because four places had their own copy of these four strings** — the writer's `Prepare`, the writer's `ReadExisting`, [`SetReader`](Nfty.Core.Output.SetReader.md), and [`SetReader.IsSetFolder()`](Nfty.Core.Output.SetReader.md#m-issetfolder-system-string) — and a fifth was about to be added by `SetWriter.Pack`, which is the one that has to be exactly right. A Set folder is a folder the user chose, so the only thing separating "the Set" from "everything else the user keeps there" is this list.

**It is an INCLUDE list, and that direction is the whole point.** `Pack` used to zip every file under the output folder and merely exclude a top-level `.set`, which is unbounded in exactly the wrong direction: cooking into a Kitchen — a folder whose entire purpose is to hold loose `.cbk`, `.rcp` and `.igt` parts — packed the author's complete source into the archive they were about to hand a buyer. No exclusion list can enumerate what a person might leave in a folder; a description of what a Set IS can. It is the same rule `Archives.KindOf` follows in refusing an unknown extension rather than guessing at it.

The three directories are taken WHOLE rather than filtered by extension. They are nfty's own namespace inside the user's folder, so the boundary that matters is the directory, not the file type — and filtering on `.png` would silently drop an asset the day the format grows a second image encoding.

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<string> Directories { get; }
```

The subdirectories taken whole, in the order a listing reads best. `models/` is deliberately NOT here: it belongs to a Set only as far as `set.json` says ([`SetLayout.ModelFilesIn()`](Nfty.Core.Output.SetLayout.md#m-modelfilesin-system-string)), because a folder named `models` is a name an art workspace plausibly already uses.

## Methods

### FilesIn(string) { #m-filesin-system-string }

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<string> FilesIn(string setDir);
```

Every file that belongs to the Set in `setDir`, and nothing else in that folder.

**Parameters**

- `setDir` (`string`) - The Set folder.

**Returns.** Paths relative or absolute as `setDir`, in `Ordinal` order. Ordinal because these reach an output file: the default comparer sorts by the current culture, so the same Set would pack to a different archive on an `en-US` machine than on a `sv-SE` one — the rule every other sort that reaches disk here already follows.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException` - `setDir` is null or whitespace.

### ModelFilesIn(string) { #m-modelfilesin-system-string }

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<string> ModelFilesIn(string setDir);
```

The model files `set.json` in `setDir` accounts for: for a Set that recorded a `models` block, `NNNN.glb` (or `.gltf` and `.bin` per the recorded format) for each numbered asset that was not recorded as skipped. Nothing else in `models/`, and nothing at all for a Set without the block.

**Parameters**

- `setDir` (`string`) - The Set folder.

**Returns.** Paths relative or absolute as `setDir`, in `Ordinal` order.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException` - `setDir` is null or whitespace.

**Remarks**

This is the one rule for "which of the folder's `models/` is the Set's": the listing, `Pack`, the exporter and the export dialog all ask here, so a user's own `models/secret-source.blend` - or a stray `0001.glb` beside a Set cooked without models - cannot ride along into a buyer's archive.

### Stem(int) { #m-stem-system-int32 }

```csharp
public static string Stem(int number);
```

The name an asset's files share, without extension: its set number padded to four digits (growing past 9,999), invariant so no culture's digits or sign ever reach a file name.

**Parameters**

- `number` (`int`) - The asset's number within the Set.

**Returns.** For example `0042`.
